claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're responsible for.

Let me start with a basic question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 6 years old. I was wondering if I could claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son **Alex**, who is 6 years old. That's helpful.

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand your living situation better.

**Do you live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his mother.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with his mother, I need to understand your financial involvement in supporting him.

**Are you currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep, such as money for his food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with things like his clothes, school supplies, and other expenses he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Since you're making contributions towards Alex's upkeep, I need to understand the level and consistency of these contributions.

**Are your contributions to Alex's upkeep at least equal to the current Child Benefit payment amount (which is £25.60 per week for the first child), and do you make these contributions regularly?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute regularly. I give about £30 a week to help with his expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information. I have one more important question to ensure I have the full picture:

**Does Alex's mother currently claim Child Benefit for him, or have you agreed between yourselves who will claim it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His mother doesn't claim Child Benefit for him currently, so there's no issue with that. We haven't really discussed who would claim it - I just wanted to find out if I'm eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the rules and your circumstances:

- Alex is 6 years old (under 16) ✓
- You don't live with Alex, but you are making regular financial contributions of £30 per week towards his upkeep ✓
- These contributions meet or exceed the Child Benefit payment amount ✓
- Alex's mother is not currently claiming Child Benefit for him ✓

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can be responsible for a child even if you don't live with them, as long as you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them. Your regular contributions of £30 per week satisfy this requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!** 

Your regular contributions of £30 per week towards his upkeep demonstrate financial responsibility, which is sufficient to qualify you for Child Benefit even though he lives with his mother. Since she's not currently claiming it, you can proceed with making a claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
